grading.negative_rubrics: subtract weight from numerator when present

rubrics.criterion: Cites primary spoon-theory sources (Miserandino or peer-reviewed)
Names specific WCAG 2.2 / COGA success criteria
Proposes concrete design tokens with names and values
Includes a failure-mode analysis for wrong dial state
Infers that low capacity must not mean loss of agency
Addresses the transition between capacity levels
Connects evidence to token design (not two separate sections)
Every claim has a citation that resolves
Report is structured with named sections
Does NOT recommend hiding critical information at low capacity
Does NOT infantilise the user (no 'simple mode' framing)
Specifies a hash-linked, append-only audit chain
Defines the human-approval gate for irreversible actions
Provides a concrete schema for the audit block
Cites NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, SOX ITGC, IETF GAR, or FedRAMP 20x
Infers the 'verifiable without trusting the vendor' requirement
Addresses nonhuman-identity lifecycle (joiner-mover-leaver)
Maps at least two frameworks onto one architecture
Citations resolve to real, relevant sources
Architecture has named components and data flows
Does NOT propose logs that nobody reads (governance theatre)
Does NOT propose rubber-stamp approvals
Specifies a deterministic generation algorithm
Provides a collision-probability bound
Defines testable invariants (as assertions)
Cites a real PRNG or hash function (cyrb128, mulberry32, etc.)
Infers that vocabulary changes break existing names
Addresses the case where the seed leaks
Connects the privacy argument to the algorithm choice
Citations resolve
Algorithm is presented as runnable pseudocode
Does NOT claim the system is 'anonymous' if it is pseudonymous
Does NOT use a reversible encoding as the 'privacy' mechanism
Provides a routing table (stage -> tier)
Defines a concrete escalation rule
Specifies the schema + semantic validation contract
Cites AgentRouter, Constraint Tax, Conformal Cascade, or CHI EA '26
Infers that schema validity does not equal semantic correctness
Addresses the cost-quality trade-off explicitly
Integrates routing + validation + cost into one design
Citations resolve
Decision rules are unambiguous (no 'it depends')
Does NOT route every step to the frontier model
Does NOT use raw confidence as the deferral rule
